page: Microsoft Azure E96-24ads_v7 is a constrained-core memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz, delivering 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU supports modern instruction sets including AVX-512 extensions (f, vnni, and bf16) as well as hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The architecture includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache.

A central architectural feature is the massive memory allocation paired with high-capacity local storage. The system features 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding an extensive memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture includes 5,670 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage, providing substantial low-latency temporary capacity. The instance includes no GPU acceleration and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core compute alongside high memory throughput. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests and fast single-threaded compression throughput (41.36 GB/sec for gzip compression and 18.14 GB/sec for bzip3 decompression). In multi-core stress-ng and PassMark CPU testing, the 24-vCPU allocation places performance in the middle 50% tier, while PassMark memory testing registers in the upper quartile. Read-only cached memory bandwidth reaches 2,592.04 GB/sec, with large-block memory read bandwidth sustained at 103.44 GB/sec.

The constrained-core layout of the E96-24ads_v7 offers distinct qualitative cost efficiency for software stacks licensed per core that demand massive memory capacities. By provisioning only 24 active vCPUs against a 768 GB memory footprint, it controls per-core licensing expenses while maximizing in-memory caching capacity. This configuration is ideally suited for enterprise database engines, in-memory caches like Redis, ETL pipelines processing memory-resident data sets, and memory-constrained analytical applications.
